documented_diagnosis.name: Squamous cell carcinoma
documented_diagnosis.evidence: Confirmed by biopsy, as recorded in PAD-UFES-20.

teaching_points: Squamous cell carcinoma often appears as a firm pink or red bump with scale or crust on sun-exposed skin.
It can grow over weeks to months and can spread, so early assessment matters.
Older age, fair skin and long-term sun exposure raise the risk.

look_alikes.name: Keratoacanthoma
look_alikes.note: Grows quickly into a dome with a central keratin plug.

look_alikes.name: Hypertrophic actinic keratosis
look_alikes.note: Thick scale on a flatter base.

look_alikes.name: Basal cell carcinoma
look_alikes.note: Pearly and translucent rather than scaly.
